name: CA-46
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Correa holds a roughly $2.5M-to-$6K cash advantage
District leans Democratic by about 10 points
No polls or expert ratings indicate a competitive race
Prediction markets price Correa's win odds around 95%
model.rationale: Correa combines incumbency, a district that leans about ten points Democratic, and an overwhelming financial edge over a first-time challenger who has raised under $81,000. With no polls or ratings suggesting competitiveness and markets pricing the race near 95% Democratic, nothing justifies moving off the fundamentals-based outlook.
model.watch: A late scandal involving Correa, significant outside spending for Pan, or a sharply unfavorable national environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lou Correa, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a Southern California district that leans about ten points Democratic. He advanced past the top-two primary and faces Republican David Pan, a first-time candidate with minimal financial backing. Correa has raised roughly $1.2 million and holds about $2.5 million on hand, while Pan has raised about $81,000 with under $7,000 available, leaving the challenger little capacity to introduce himself to voters.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the spending gap. Prediction markets put Correa's chances around 95 percent. Barring an unexpected scandal or major outside intervention, the seat is expected to remain comfortably in Democratic hands in November.
